source_attestations.note: Rules attestation (14 items, all PASS) re-verified

summary:
Sauron, Lord of the Rings is an eight-drop whose cast trigger amasses, mills five and reanimates even if he's countered. The list is a reanimator deck (Entomb, Buried Alive, Animate Dead, Reanimate, Metamorphosis Fanatic, Living Death), with Anger and Wonder working from the graveyard, Sneak Attack, and a four-Nazgûl Ring side engine. Fast mana (Mana Vault, Grim Monolith) is there only to cast him sooner. There are no Spellbook lines. All 14 attestation items are re-verified against the canonical list.

Rules surprises: countering Sauron doesn't stop the reanimation; the return can pick any creature card in your graveyard and is mandatory; Living Death doesn't bring back your Army token or Sauron; four Nazgûl are legal in Commander. No list errors.

interactions.title: Cast trigger: amass 5, mill 5, then reanimate (resolves even if Sauron is countered)
interactions.ruling: Sauron's first ability triggers when he's cast, from the command zone or from hand. It resolves before Sauron himself and works on its own, so countering the Sauron spell doesn't stop it. In order, it amasses Orcs 5, mills five, then returns a creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield. That can be a card already there or one just milled. The return is mandatory if you have a creature card. Command Beacon puts him in hand. Casting him from there has no commander tax, still triggers, and doesn't add to the tax.
interactions.short: Cast trigger is independent of the spell; the reanimation picks from the whole graveyard after the mill.

oracle.quote: When you cast this spell, amass Orcs 5, mill five cards, then return a creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield.

rulings.quote: The creature card you choose doesn't need to be a card you milled. You may choose a creature card that was already in your graveyard before you milled.

If you cast a commander from your hand, the additional cost based on the number of times you've cast it from your command zone (sometimes referred to as the "commander tax") doesn't apply. Additionally, that casting won't add to the tax if you later cast the commander from the command zone.

interactions.title: Reanimation chains: Metamorphosis Fanatic, Dance of the Dead, Animate Dead, Necromancy, Reanimate
interactions.ruling: If Sauron's trigger returns Metamorphosis Fanatic, its ETB returns up to one more creature card with a lifelink counter, so you get two bodies from one cast. Entomb and Buried Alive set up the graveyard. Dance of the Dead returns its creature tapped with +1/+1. That creature doesn't untap normally, but you can pay {1}{B} in your upkeep to untap it. If Dance leaves the battlefield, the creature is sacrificed.

oracle.quote: When this creature enters, return up to one target creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield with a lifelink counter on it.

rulings.quote: This is a new wording. Dance of the Dead is now an Aura. You target a creature card in a graveyard when you cast it. It enters attached to that card. Then it returns that card to the battlefield, and attaches itself to that card again (since the card is treated as a new object on the battlefield).

interactions.title: Living Death: exile, sacrifice, return. Tokens and Sauron don't come back
interactions.ruling:
Living Death resolves in three steps, each happening for all players at once:
1. Exile every creature card from every graveyard.
2. Sacrifice every creature on the battlefield.
3. Put the exiled cards onto the battlefield.

Only cards exiled in step 1 return. Your Orc Army token and Sauron himself are sacrificed in step 2 and don't return; Sauron can go to the command zone. Sacrifice creatures beforehand with Phyrexian Tower ({B}{B}, a mana ability) so they're in the graveyard for step 1. Sneak Attack's end-step sacrifice also stocks the graveyard.
interactions.short: Only creature cards already in graveyards return; your Army token and Sauron are just sacrificed.

oracle.quote: Each player exiles all creature cards from their graveyard, then sacrifices all creatures they control, then puts all cards they exiled this way onto the battlefield.

rulings.quote: Only cards exiled by Living Death's first instruction are put onto the battlefield. If a replacement effect (such as that of Leyline of the Void) causes any of the sacrificed creatures to be exiled instead of put into a graveyard, those cards aren't returned to the battlefield.
You sacrifice the creature only if you still control it. If that creature has left the battlefield, even if it came back, you don't sacrifice it.

interactions.title: Four Nazgûl are legal; each temptation grows every Wraith once per Nazgûl
interactions.ruling: Nazgûl's own text lets a deck run up to nine copies, overriding the singleton rule. The canonical list runs four. Each Nazgûl's ETB has the Ring tempt you, and each Nazgûl triggers on every temptation. With k Nazgûl out, one temptation puts k counters on each Wraith. Sauron's trigger when an opponent's commander dies is another temptation, and it happens even if that commander goes to the command zone. The Ring can tempt you even if you control no creatures.
interactions.short: Up to 9 Nazgûl allowed; each temptation = +k counters per Wraith with k Nazgûl.

oracle.quote: A deck can have up to nine cards named Nazgûl.
Whenever the Ring tempts you, put a +1/+1 counter on each Wraith you control.

rulings.quote: The last ability of Nazgûl also lets you ignore the "singleton" rule in formats like Commander.
Sauron, Lord of the Rings's last ability will trigger even if the owner of the commander that died chooses to return it to the command zone after it dies.

interactions.title: Anger and Wonder work from the graveyard, if you control a Mountain or Island
interactions.ruling: Sauron's mill can bin Anger and Wonder. From your graveyard, Anger gives your creatures haste while you control a Mountain, and Wonder gives flying while you control an Island. Typed duals count, and Anger works even if you had no Mountain when it was milled. The Mouth of Sauron can target you: mill three, then amass Orcs equal to the instants and sorceries in your graveyard.

oracle.quote: As long as this card is in your graveyard and you control a Mountain, creatures you control have haste.

When The Mouth of Sauron enters, target player mills three cards. Then amass Orcs X, where X is the number of instant and sorcery cards in that player's graveyard. (Put X +1/+1 counters on an Army you control. It's also an Orc. If you don't control an Army, create a 0/0 black Orc Army creature token first.)

rulings.quote: The timestamp for the "in your graveyard" ability is set at the time that this card goes to your graveyard, regardless of whether you control a Mountain at that time.
